title: Create API Keys Database Schema
description: Define and implement the database schema for storing API keys with proper security considerations
details: Create a new `apiKeys` table in the Drizzle schema with columns: `id` (primary key), `userId` (foreign key to users table), `name` (user-defined key name), `hashedKey` (SHA-256 hashed version of the key), `keyPrefix` (first 8 characters for identification), `lastFourChars` (last 4 characters for user identification), `createdAt`, and `expiresAt` (optional). Use proper indexing on userId for efficient queries. Implement the migration script to create this table in the database. Ensure foreign key constraints are properly set up to maintain referential integrity with the users table.
test_strategy: Write unit tests to verify schema definition is correct, test database migration runs successfully, and validate that foreign key constraints work properly. Test that the table can be created and queried through Drizzle ORM.

title: Implement API Keys Backend Endpoints
description: Create secure API routes for generating, storing, and retrieving API keys
details: Create `app/api/keys/route.ts` with GET and POST handlers. The POST handler should: verify user authentication via Better Auth, validate input (key name), generate a cryptographically secure 32-byte random key using Node.js crypto module, create a key prefix (e.g., 'sk_' + first 8 chars), hash the full key using SHA-256 with salt, store the hashed version in database, and return the full unhashed key to client (only once). The GET handler should retrieve all keys for the authenticated user, returning only safe data (id, name, keyPrefix, lastFourChars, createdAt). Implement proper error handling for database failures and authentication errors.
test_strategy: Unit test key generation logic, hashing functions, and database operations. Test authentication middleware integration. Verify that raw keys are never stored and that GET requests don't expose sensitive data. Test error scenarios like invalid sessions and database failures.

title: Build API Key Management UI Component
description: Create a React component for managing API keys with create, view, and copy functionality
details: Create `components/dashboard/api-key-manager.tsx` using shadcn/ui components. Include: a list view showing existing keys (name, prefix + last 4 chars, created date), a '+ Create New Key' button, a Dialog component with a form for entering key name, success state showing the generated key with copy-to-clipboard functionality, and loading/error states. Use React hooks for state management and API calls. Implement proper TypeScript interfaces for API responses. Add visual indicators for key identification (prefix + masked middle + last 4 chars). Include clear messaging that keys are only shown once.
test_strategy: Test component rendering with different states (loading, error, success). Verify form validation and submission. Test copy-to-clipboard functionality across different browsers. Mock API calls and test error handling scenarios.

title: Integrate API Key Manager into Dashboard
description: Add the API key management component to the main dashboard page with proper layout and navigation
details: Modify `app/dashboard/page.tsx` to include the new ApiKeyManager component. Create a dedicated section or tab for API key management within the existing dashboard layout. Ensure the component is properly positioned and styled to match the existing dashboard design. Add appropriate loading states and error boundaries. Implement proper responsive design for different screen sizes. Consider adding a navigation item or quick access button if the dashboard has a sidebar or navigation menu.
test_strategy: Test integration with existing dashboard layout and ensure no styling conflicts. Verify responsive design on different screen sizes. Test navigation flow and ensure the feature is discoverable. Perform end-to-end testing of the complete user flow from dashboard access to key creation.
